findings.title: A Word document in. Structured Markdown out.
findings.summary: A freshly generated Word document became Markdown with its heading and table cell contents intact. The complete conversion ran locally in the network-disabled sandbox, with no LLM client configured.
checks: A level-1 Word heading became “# My Test Heading”.
All four table values survived in Markdown table rows: Name, Value, Alpha, and 42.
limitations: One simple DOCX file was tested. Nested or merged tables, images, styles, and malformed documents were not tested.
The output adds an empty Markdown header row. This establishes preservation of the table content, not identical formatting or header semantics.
The source checkout was installed in editable mode with its DOCX dependencies. No explicit repository commit hash was captured.
findings.review_note: The presentation is based on the actual command output. The original inconclusive investigation is preserved below; it is not overwritten by this rerun. This finding makes no licensing claim.
findings.repo_description: Microsoft’s Python tool for converting documents into Markdown, a plain-text document format.
findings.claim: A Word document can be converted to Markdown while preserving its heading and table contents, without an LLM API.
findings.test_description: Created a DOCX file with one heading and a 2×2 table, then ran MarkItDown’s default converter in a Docker sandbox with runtime network access disabled.

findings.title: Typed output, tested beyond the happy path.
findings.summary: Pydantic AI returned a declared City model for valid test output. Deliberately invalid output triggered the library’s output-retry error. Both checks ran against the actual library using its local TestModel backend.
findings.method: Automatic selection from a saved batch · Docker execution
checks: Valid test output returned an actual City model instance.
An integer in a string field triggered UnexpectedModelBehavior after the output retry limit.
limitations: Only the synchronous local TestModel backend was exercised. Real LLM providers, async execution, and streaming were not tested.
The negative test prints its exception rather than asserting its exact type. Its recorded stdout supplies the observed result.
No separate type-coercion case or full repository language audit was performed. No explicit source commit hash was captured.
findings.review_note: The original automated report uses stronger wording about pure Python and coercion. This reviewed presentation narrows the conclusion to the two observed validation behaviors; the original remains unedited in the evidence below.
findings.repo_description: A Python library for building AI agents with structured outputs validated against Pydantic schemas.
findings.claim: An agent configured with a structured output type returns a matching model for valid data and rejects data that violates the schema.
findings.test_description: Ran the library with its local TestModel backend and a City schema containing two string fields. Tested valid data, then supplied an integer for one field and inspected the resulting error.
